properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/09/2021 to ARD OPR LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/09/2021
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 925830
Permit API: 081-21877
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/09/2021
Comments: On August 9, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response to a spill at EQT COP Tract 551 Pad B. The spill of drilling mud outside of containment was reported on August 6, 2021. The DEP staff met with EQT company man R.D. Mann. Mr. Mann showed the DEP where the spill occurred and explained that a mud line ruptured outside containment. The area had already been excavated and the impacted soil had been removed prior to the inspection. Two ditches were dug to remove the impacted soil and the impacted soil was removed and back filled on the traveling lane of the well pad. The ditch 1 dug was about 20 feet by 3 feet and about 3 feet deep. Ditch 2 was about 15 ft by 4 feet and about 2 feet deep. The estimation of the amount of oil based mud was about 4.2 barrels spilled, not 42 gallons as the detail sheet states. The spill occurred near the sump and french drain that had been dug for a prior release. The DEP recommended vacuuming the water out of Ditch 1 prior to back filling. Another area of the well pad had been scraped to allow water that is leeching from under the secondary containment of the drilling rig to pool and be vacuumed. The water that is leaching from under the containment is from a previously discovered brine spill. The conductivity of the water in the pool was 848 uS/cm. The DEP recommends monitoring the conductivity of the water that becomes pooled. Precision Drilling 110 is onsite and in the process of drilling the fourth well out of nine wells planned for the well pad. Secondary containment berms and liner where it could be observed was in good condition. There were 4 cement silos and 14 baker tanks onsite in secondary containment. The release of drilling mud outside of containment is violation of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Violations remain outstanding from Inspection Report 3207564.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/03/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/03/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8284090
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2026
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

properties.content:

Violation ID: 8275606
Permit API: 051-21601
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Luzerne Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/18/2026
Comments: On May 18, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4180049.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. The stage of plugging operations was not confirmed during this inspection. The rig has been removed from the site at this time. The well head is observed in the well cellar.During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S plan is on site. The E and S plan has not been updated to depict the stream that runs under the access road. - Plastic matting has been removed from all three locations along the access road and from on site. - Disturbance along the access road is observed in multiple areas which appears to be due to vehicle traffic (Photos 4-8, 11-14). The Department recommends the operator repair the disturbance during site restoration.- Sedimentation observed in previous inspection remains visible along the access road above the culvert outlet (Photo 9). The Department recommends the operator return the sediment to the access road and install E and S BMPs above the culvert to prevent sedimentation to the stream channel. - The stream channel (Photo 10) appears to be dry at this time. - The timber mat bridge at the site entrance appears to have been removed (Photo 15).- CFS on the well site appears to be improperly implemented/maintained in two areas (Photos 16-17). The Department recommends the operator ensure CFS is staked with no more than 10 feet between each stake. - Soil stockpile is osberved to be experiencing some vegetative growth on the back side (Photo 20).- Well cellar is observed and well tag/posting requirements are met on site. - Pump jack remains on site at this time. Violations are being continued for failure to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, failure to identify a stream on the E and S plan, failure to implement/maintain E and S BMPs, and accelerated erosion and sedimentation off of the access road. Violations were also continued in IR 4201247 for staining still observed near twp previously observed minor releases of petroleum products and/or brine.

Comments: On site today in response to a water complaint in the area. This is a FUI (Follow Up Inspection) for the (4) wells on the pad that were inspected on 10/14/21. Remedial work was completed on the 2H, 4H and 6H wells at the end of 2017 to address previous violations cited on the 6H well. - Met w/ lease operator Ben Whitaker to perform isolated gas screenings of the cemented annuli. - All (4) wells have the (20x13) and (13x9) annuli isolated and venting to atmosphere. No gas flow was detected at any of these wells (20x13) or (13x9) cemented annuli. - The (20x13) and (13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad were left open and venting to atmosphere upon completion of gas screenings and flow checks. - Individual prod. casing pressures listed below: - 2H: 631 psi., capillary string - 4H: 618 psi., capillary string - 6H: 658 psi., capillary string - 8H: 660 psi. ** Although gas was detected at the (20x13) cemented annuli of the 6H and the 8H wells, no flow was detected via Cabots O&G's ALICAT micro flow meter. This appears to remain indicative of commingling, residual gas within the vent lines and/ or annular spaces. On 9/3/2020 The Dept. requested that Cabot assess these conditions further and contact the Dept. with Cabots assessments. On 6/26/2021 Cabot O&G submitted a "Gas Migration Final Report" including a summary of previous remedial work performed on wells and an assessment of these residual gas detections. - No other violations or obvious concerns were noted.

Violation ID: 8205345
Permit API: 051-24210
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: Nicholson Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/18/2024
Comments: On October 18 2024 the Department conducted an inspection in regards to a spill reported under CTS 384608. Present during the inspection were operator representatives Paul Stiner and Bryan Goletz.The findings are as follows:Upon talking to the operator while onsite, it was stated that a check valve had broke causing a pressure build up to occur in the underground poly flow line, resulting in the line to fail. The failure in the poly line caused roughly 55 barrels of brine to be released into the ground. The release was observed by the operator at roughly 12 pm on 10/18/24, and reported to the Department at 1:17pm on 10/18/2024 . While onsite, the Department observed Penn Plus onsite beginning remediation efforts. According to Mr.Stiner, triaxle trucks are to arrive to the site on 10/21/2024, and all impacted soil would be excavated and disposed of. The operator stated because of the size of the release, they will be under going Act 2 remediation, with Moody preparing all of the related Act 2 documents/reports.Upon inspection of the location of the spill, the Department observed what appeared to be the location of the failure in the poly line (photos 1 and 2). A conductivity reading was taken in this location with a reading of "OR" (Out of range of maximum readings).The Department observed puddles of fluid on the surface of the well site (photos 5-7). The Department observed a tanker truck onsite using suction hoses to remove the excess fluid/puddles from the ground. Conductivity readings were taken with in the puddles as well as downslope from the location of the poly line failure with multiple readings of "OR". Elevated readings (9.22mS) were detected roughly 175 feet down slope (east) of the failure. Mr.Stiner stated he had obtained elevated readings approximately 180 feet from the poly line failure and the depth of contamination appeared to be roughly 2 feet (photo 14). No impacts to waters of the commonwealth were observed.The Department recommends the operator follows the Department's Spill Policy and October 3 2014 Program Clarification Memo for remediation of the spill. The Department requests the waste manifest for the impacted material upon receipt.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release.This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery.Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned.Based on todays inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Violation ID: 910655
Permit API: 047-24039
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/16/2021
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report from the operator of a brine leak at the tank battery of the #38448 well location (CID #355324). It appears as though ice accumulated within the diking and dislodged the drain line from the stock tank to the brine tank, allowing the tank to drain into the diking. Most of the fluid remained in containment, but a portion flowed out at a point of failure that had previously been noted in a 12/30/19 inspection of this site that had not been fixed. Elevated conductivity, in some places as high as >20 mS, was noted in puddles on the north and southwest corners of the site, and in the soil along the berm on the west side of the containment. The operator reported that 40 barrels of brine was released to containment. It is uncertain how much brine leaked outside of containment, but it is likely <1 barrel. The operator has disconnected the line from both tanks, closed the valves and put a bull plug in each. Per a phone call with Kirk Elkin of Diversified, they have already removed ~25 barrels of brine via vac truck, and will be mobilizing equipment to collect the rest of the brine and contaminated soil the week of 3/22/21. Further followup inspection will be done at that time.

Comments: On February 26, 2019, the Department performed an inspection of CNX/Diversified Energy E Rinehart#9 well site. The site is located in Jackson Twp., Greene Co. The inspection was related to a reported brine release from valve on a brine tank by the operator. The operator reported a spill of approximately 22 BBLs of brine from a brine water transfer line on 2/25/19. The operator reported that a valve at the brine storage tank in an earthen dike has broken releasing the brine into the earthen dike. The operator has reported that the brine was captured and stored in the earthen dike around the tanks. At time of inspection standing brine was noted in the dike and the soil conductivity readings in the dike were Over Readings (Or) or greater than 20 mS. Oil stained/saturated soil was noted near the well head and production equipment.

Permit API: 047-24039
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/16/2021
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report from the operator of a brine leak at the tank battery of the #38448 well location (CID #355324). It appears as though ice accumulated within the diking and dislodged the drain line from the stock tank to the brine tank, allowing the tank to drain into the diking. Most of the fluid remained in containment, but a portion flowed out at a point of failure that had previously been noted in a 12/30/19 inspection of this site that had not been fixed. Elevated conductivity, in some places as high as >20 mS, was noted in puddles on the north and southwest corners of the site, and in the soil along the berm on the west side of the containment. The operator reported that 40 barrels of brine was released to containment. It is uncertain how much brine leaked outside of containment, but it is likely <1 barrel. The operator has disconnected the line from both tanks, closed the valves and put a bull plug in each. Per a phone call with Kirk Elkin of Diversified, they have already removed ~25 barrels of brine via vac truck, and will be mobilizing equipment to collect the rest of the brine and contaminated soil the week of 3/22/21. Further followup inspection will be done at that time.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/08/2024 to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/08/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8186932
Permit API: 081-21938
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/08/2024
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted following a reported release of produced fluid to the pad surface from 3/1/24. A workover rig is in operation drilling out plugs on the well pad following fracing operations. Equipment for the frac has mostly been removed from the location. Additional equipment was being hauled away during this inspection. I met with EQT company man Marc McCartor at the beginning of this inspection. The area of the pad surface which was impacted by the 3/1/24 release appeared dry without any visible staining. Fluid is present in the stormwater channel along the northwest pad edge. The fluid is present in the channel from the approximate halfway point of the pad edge to the compost filter sock infiltration berm at the west corner of the pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid is 4.46 mS/cm near the halfway point of the pad edge. Approximately 25 feet west within the channel, the EC peaked at 10.23 mS/cm and then gradually decreased as it headed farther west within the channel. The EC of the fluid where the path of the fluid ended at the compost filter sock berm at the west corner is 2.43 mS/cm. I notified the company man about the elevated EC fluid in the stormwater channel and then took sample 0718-237 from the fluid in the stormwater channel at 1242. The sample was sent to the state laboratory on the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. I left a voicemail for EQT representative Rick Hall at 1338 on the same day to let him know of my findings. Later that day at 1555 I spoke with EQT representative Zac Subra. He told me that an internal investigation found that a contractor was flushing lines which had contained produced fluid following fracing operations. The contractor released what they believed to be freshwater which actually contained some portion of produced fluid. Mr. Subra said that they believe that this was the origin of the fluid in the channel and that EQT intends to pursue Act 2 remediation for this release. He also stated that a vacuum truck was already on site removing the fluid with elevated electrical conductivity. He said Penn E and R and Tobias Excavation was en route to the site to characterize and excavate the impacted material, respectively. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Violations noted for this release against permit 081-21946.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21938 for the 3/1/24 produced fluid release.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/09/2026 to COPPERHEAD ENTERPRISES LLC in Hamilton Township, McKean county. SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: COPPERHEAD ENTERPRISES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/09/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8280934
Permit API: 083-47442
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/09/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to being notified by Chuck Rippey of Copperhead Enterprises on 7/8/26 of a crude oil spill due to a compromised subsurface gathering line located at the entrance of the spur road that accesses this conventional well. At the time of notification, according to Chuck, all wells on the lease had been shut in and containment measures were being placed throughout the impacted area.At the onset of this inspection, I met with Chuck who explained that the gathering line failed due to valves on the gathering lines at the tank battery unknowingly being closed by a suspected, unknown, third party prior to the lease being pumped on the afternoon of 7/8/26. It is estimated that the wells on the lease were pumping for 2-3 hours before the well tender drove towards this well and noticed the release at approximately 15:00. After ceasing production and shutting in the wells, Chuck reported the release to this WQSS via telephone.At the origin of the release, crude oil had sprayed onto the road bank and lower limbs of nearby trees. The majority of the crude oil migrated west/ northwest in a roadside ditch alongside Chappel Fork Road for approximately 400' before reaching a spring run that evolves into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Chappel Fork. Pockets of crude oil were observed in the spring run/UNT between where it intersects Chappel Fork Road and its confluence with Chappel Fork. Crude oil was also present in an approximate 750' stretch of Chappel Fork downslope of the stream's confluence with the aforementioned spring run/UNT.At this time, underflow dams, absorbent booms and pads have been placed throughout the impacted portions of the roadside ditch, spring run/UNT and Chappel Fork to contain the released product. Crews were in the process of recovering crude that was collecting behind the various containment measures and replacing saturated absorbents as needed. I advised Chuck to continue the ongoing practices and to place additional booms in slow moving water to minimize the potential for further migration downstream. After further progress is made with recovering the free crude, Chuck intends to excavate the contaminated soil at the origin of the release and replace the ruptured portion of the gathering line.At this time, the quantity of crude oil that was released is unknown. Chuck intends to stage the excavated contaminated soil on a lined pod at this well site until proper disposal at a landfill is arranged. Documentation of this disposal and confirmatory sampling of the impacted area after its remediation is expected to be provided to the Department in order for this incident to be considered closed.Upcoming inspections will be done throughout the remediation of this release to ensure suitable progress is being made.

Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 8232155
Permit API: 125-28458
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Smith Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/01/2025
Comments: On May 1, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the Malinky well pad in Smith Township, Washington County. According to the incident report that was submitted by Range Resources representative Nate Smiell, approximately 200 gallons of diethylene glycol was released to the surface of the well pad on the day of this inspection at 11:27 AM. No waterways are reported to have been impacted and remediation crew is on the way for cleanup. This spill report was submitted to the Department on the day of this inspection at 12:45 PM. Mr. Smiell was present onsite for this inspection. Additional representatives from Range Resources and SPSI were also onsite conducting remediation.Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Smiell who further explained that diethylene glycol was being pumped from the GPU units in preparation for installation of secondary containment, per the requirements of an active Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) between the operator and the Department, when the pump truck operator erroneously pumped the diethylene glycol from the GPU into a chamber of the truck tank that was already full. This resulted in an estimated 200 gallons of diethylene glycol being released from a vent on the top of the truck's vessel and to the surface of well pad. Three spill cleanup drums were filled with absorbent material that soaked up the standing ethylene glycol on the well pad surface. Two rolloff boxes are expected to be required to contain the impacted material. Mr. Smiell then confirmed that the operator will conduct remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2. Mr. Smiell reported that at the time of this inspection, the majority of the impacted material appears to have been removed. This is based on testing that was conducted by Mr. Smiell throughout the impacted area, utilizing a glycol test kit, however a third-party environmental consultant is scheduled to take confirmation samples on the day following this inspection, per the requirements of Act 2. Excavation and remediation of the impacted area remains ongoing at the time of inspection (see photos 4-8, 12, and 17-19). The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Some minor potholes were observed in the access road (see photo 2). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 3). No Safety Data Sheet (SDS) was located onsite for diethylene glycol, the pollutant released during this incident. The GPU units are in the process of being equipped with secondary containment (see photo 9). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 10). Violation ID: 890376
Permit API: 047-23569
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Saint Marys City
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 07/31/2020
Comments: The operator called the Department to report a spill that was found the morning of 7/31/2020. Per the operator, a leak of brine occurred from a poly tank or the line leading from the separator to the tank and leaked into containment. It then ran around a freshwater drain pipe that was placed in at construction.The well is an open flowing well that appears to in production, with the valves opened. The well is plumbed to a gas separator and a 50 barrel poly tank within containment. Some stained soil is apparent between the separator and the containment, with elevated conductivity >1mS noted using a Soil EC meter probe. Vegetation within the containment is distressed or dead, indicating brine discharge. Down slope from the containment, vegetation has been killed in a band consistent with discharge from or around the freshwater drain. Conductivity measured ~11 mS near the drain and diminished down slope, with the final reading over 1 mS noted approximately 100 feet from the tank, in a scour location that was likely from a stormwater event. The total volume of brine leaked is likely close to the Operator's estimate of 30-35 gallons, with approximately 5-10 gallons being outside containment.The operator was called back. They said that they would have a contractor on site to dig up impacted soil early next week. Followup inspection will be dome then.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-10-03
Comments: Inspection completed in response to a notification received from the operator on October 2, 2019 of a release discovered on the same day. The operator stated in the notification that they believe that a can containing secondary containment leaked produced water onto compromised secondary containment which caused a release to the pad surface. The operator estimated the volume of release at 2 barrels. DEP Compliance Specialist Chris Southard accompanied me on this inspection. We met with Mike Deming and Anthony Mauro, both with SWN, on location. Mr. Deming and Mr. Mauro informed us that some excavation was done on Oct. 2nd but it was stopped due to rain. They said that they plan to resume excavation on Oct. 4th. They showed us the area to the south and east of the well heads that they believe was impacted by the release. This area did have electrical conductivity readings which were elevated comapred to the rest of the pad. We walked the site with Mr. Deming. We walked around the infiltration basin to the south of the pad as well but could not find any water in the basin, nor in the rock-lined ditch which leads to the basin, to screen. Due to the estimated volume of the release, the Department recommends pursing Act 2. Violations noted.

2019-11-15
Report Details
Operator: Rockdale Marcellus Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-11-15
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 869021
Permit API: 117-21999
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-11-15
Comments: Inspection conducted in response to a notification from the operator about a release of glycol to the pad surface. I met with Jim Bastion with Principle Energy upon arriving on location. Mr. Bastion showed me the area where the release occurred near the produced water tanks. The area had already had impacted material scrapped from the surface. Mr. Bastion stated that the release was not glycol but actually a food-grade oil which is being utilized as a heat transfer fluid to prevent produced water from freezing when it is transferred from the produced water tanks to a battery of frac tanks on location. Mr. Bastion showed me the MSDS for the fluid which did not indicate any environmental hazards. Mr. Bastion estimated the volume of release at 8 gallons. No other issues noted on the pad. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has been confirmed. Outstanding violations cited against well permit number 117-21998.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to ARG RESOURCES INC in Highland Twp, Elk County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/07/2021 to ARG RESOURCES INC in Highland Twp, Elk county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARG RESOURCES INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/07/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 920349
Permit API: 047-23879
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Highland Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/07/2021
Comments: This inspection focuses on multiple discharges from various tanks that are located in the proximity of this well. An approximate 210 bbl portable steel stock tank is actively discharging crude oil from a corroded part of the tank. The fluid is currently discharging at a minimal rate and likely only occurs during hot, sunny conditions which liquifies the residual paraffin at the bottom of the tank. At this time, there is approximately 10 gallons of free crude near the tank and a 5' x 10' area of oil soaked ground downslope of the discharge point. A second tank with the same issues is located to the south of this well. The nipple located on the bottom of a steel stock tank located west of this well has failed and resulted in an approximate 1/2 barrel of crude oil to discharge onto the ground, within an earthen containment. GPS coordinates of these incident sites are provided in the photographs included in this report. The well itself is equipped with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the location.
